- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1.00 → +1.00), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts >42.00 while true outcome is ≤40.00, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5–7 days to avoid overconfidence in high-price regime.
